newsitem.title: USA: IPO SPOTLIGHT - SeaChange could create some waves.
newsitem.headline: IPO SPOTLIGHT - SeaChange could create some waves.

text.p: SeaChange International Inc's niche appeal and digital technology could make it one of the brighter stars in this week's less-than-sparkling constellation of initial public offerings.
"They've found a niche and the market loves them," said Manish Shah, editor and publisher of the IPO Maven. "(The stock) could trade in the $17 to $19 range at the open".

Seachange, which is bringing to market two million shares in a deal managed by Morgan Stanley, provides software-based products to manage, store and distribute digital video for cable television operators and telecommunications companies.
Reflecting solid demand for the shares, the price range on the offering was raised to $14 to $16 from an initial estimated range of $12 to $14.

SeaChange's main product - the SPOT digital replacement software - allows cable operators and television broadcasters to digitally store videos such as advertisements and news updates, and then insert them automatically at very short notice into TV network streams.
"What's very appealing are the cost savings (to the customer)," said Steve Harmon, senior investment analyst at Mecklermedia. "That will get Wall Street's attention."

William Smith, analyst at Greenwich, Conn.-based Renaissance Capital Corp, agrees. As "cable operators seek lower overheads and improve performance," he said, "they are turning away from analog to digital."
Under the older analog system, where video content is stored on video tapes, changing and inserting videos is a lengthy, laborious and often costly process.
The new system allows cable operators, who have historically derived only marginal revenues from advertisements, to grab a larger share of the business from broadcast television.
Through digital technology, they can provide advertisers the tools to target communities or geographic locations with a quick turnaround time.
"They've been surviving on subscription revenues," said Shah. "This company (SeaChange) enables them to have advertisement revenues too".

The company has recently introduced a system that stores and delivers longer-form video-on-demand and pay-per-view movies. This allows viewers in hotels and apartments to choose a movie and watch it on demand.
For all its short life, SeaChange boasts a high-profile roster of customers, including Time Warner Inc, Tele-Communications Inc, and Continental Cablevision, according to its prospectus.

The company was formed in 1993 by William Styslinger, a former Digital Equipment Corp employee. It has seen its revenues soar from $5.7 million in 1994 to $23.2 million in 1995. Projected revenues for this year are about $40 million, according to Shah.

At present, there are few companies that compete directly with SeaChange. IndeNet Inc is one, and this year rolled out its own digital server. Sony Corp and Silicon Graphics Inc offer something similar, according to Smith.

While analysts see some bumps down the road as larger companies with greater resources jump on the bandwagon, they are positive about SeaChange's prospects overall. "They (SeaChange) still have a two-year window before the other guys catch up," said Shah. And after all, said Harmon, it's "not that easy to get technology and intellectual capital."

The company said in its prospectus that it plans to use the proceeds for general corporate purposes, including working capital, product development and capital expenditures. It does not see paying any cash dividends in the foreseeable future.
